newsitem.title: UK: Mayflower plans U.S. buy, to place shares.
newsitem.headline: Mayflower plans U.S. buy, to place shares.

text.p: British automotive engineering group Mayflower Plc said on Thursday it planned to buy SCSM Holdings, a large U.S. supplier of metal pressings, for $137.2 million and take up borrowings of $27.8 million.
It added that it would support the purchase with a placement of 32.83 million new shares at 126 pence each which it expected would raise net proceeds of 38.2 million pounds ($62.91 million).

SCSM, like Mayflower, specialises in pressing steel and aluminium components. Its primary U.S. markets are for light trucks and sport utility vehicles, which have been a buoyant sector of the national market for some time.
"We are delighted with the acquisition since it gives Mayflower greater critical mass in the United States," said John Simpson, chief executive of the British company.
"This is increasingly important to (automotive majors) as they continue to outsource presswork and as they seek worldwide partnerships with suppliers.
"The acquisition of SCSM furthers the group's ambitions in the U.S. market and provides an excellent platform for future growth," he added.
Due to the size of the transaction, Mayflower intends to hold an extraordinary meeting on December 2, to seek shareholder approval for the deal.
After the announcement the company's shares were up nine pence, or 6.7 percent, at 144p by 0900 GMT.
